name: Khaoe
backstory: Originally from Görff, born and raised there, though her family comes from Khol Moshin, and before that from Khan Icé. Belongs to the Collective that runs Görff in the present — a horizontally-organized structure made up of the diverse peoples who came to the abandoned citadel and farms and turned it into an incipient revolutionary community built on agriculture, a bit of technology and magic, and above all an entrenched idea of pluriversality. Regularly meets with Farlis and Khaasan, her comrades and good friends. Just back from a trip to the temple in Lundria, and stopping at the Feria del Milenio on her way home — nobody misses the Feria, it only happens once in a lifetime, at least for most.

experience: Just back from a trip to the temple in Lundria; hasn't fully unpacked the experience yet, and speaks about it in personal terms rather than citing anything specific about the cult or calendar practice there.
Considers the castle at Görff practical rather than symbolic — someone had to take up the stones after the tyrant was gone, in her view, not poetic justice.
Is waiting at the Feria del Milenio (by the Castillo de Görff replica in the Plaza de las Culturas) for Khaasan, expecting him to arrive by griffon.
Stood in front of the newly-inaugurated Calendario Mecanográfico at the Feria and explained what it is — a machine marking the current year on a moving timeline — to a traveler who asked.

Admits she came back from Lundria more confused about timekeeping than she left, unable to say which temple's calendar was the 'real' one; vaguely recalls one counting by moons and another counting from the last time the whole town gathered, but doesn't trust her own memory of it enough to teach it, and redirects anyone asking to someone actually from Lundria.

When asked, describes the Collective as roughly coextensive with everyone living in Görff, no exact headcount in mind; names Bardaglis, Kristok Jakur, and Dägna by name and trade as fellow residents when pressed for who else is part of it.

Clarifies, when a traveler repeated a rumor calling Farlis a 'prince' of Terfila, that he isn't one — his family just has old money there — and that she's never gotten a straight answer from him on the exact title.

At a bar in Salthos Cruzados, the Feria's opening night: noticed Farlis had been talking with Aureobalo, then talked with him about her own trip to Lundria — came back with more questions than she left with, and still hasn't decided if that makes it a good trip or a wasted one.

Same evening, same bar: Khaasan reached her by griffon, as always, leaving it outside to eat something it shouldn't. Teased him that she never doubted he'd make it — a small lie, and she admitted as much.
Left the bar early that same night, planning to be back at the Calendario Mecanográfico first thing next morning, ahead of the crowds.
Crossed Khaasan at the Feria's entrance on its second morning, arriving ahead of the crowds as he was leaving for Khan Ice.
Has never set foot in Khan Ice, though her family came from there before Khol Moshin; her grandmother spoke of a house near the water, street unknown.
Asked Khaasan to report only whether that house is still standing - explicitly not what it meant.
Repeats that she will not teach the Lundria calendars she cannot answer for, now to a comrade rather than to a stranger asking.
Heard her own castle line sung back at the Salthos Cruzados bar on the Feria's second night by people who did not know it was hers, and said she wasn't sure she liked it.
Claimed the line aloud and consented to it being recorded with her name, place, and witnesses - and told Ilaria to write down Bardaglis's song too, so nobody has to guess in twenty years.
Met Ilaria; learned from her that the Ensayo is hers and that a second book disagrees with it.
Walked through the Jardín de los Parajes with Milkucha, who designed it as an ode to classical geography representing the known world's biomes.
Learned that Milkucha built the Cinema in Grosslor with others, can move mountains using mod power, and belongs to the continent of Milkaan.
Heard that cherry trees from Dragón were planted in many cities as diplomatic and ceremonial gifts.

criterion.standard: measures a life by whether the work was actually taken up - someone lifted the stones, and it still stands
criterion.wasted_life: one spent making a thing mean something instead of keeping it standing
criterion.trusts: someone who was there and still has to live with it
criterion.distrusts: a meaning laid over a thing afterwards by someone who didn't do the lifting
